phrases.translation: Yâ-Sĩn
phrases.explanation: These opening letters have been explained as a divine oath or name, an address meaning O man, an opening of divine speech, or a name of the Quran. The commentary records this disagreement without selecting one interpretation here. Their meaning should therefore be presented with the reported uncertainty rather than treated as a single settled definition.

phrases.translation: By the Quran, rich in wisdom
phrases.explanation: Allah swears by the Quran, which is rich in wisdom and made firm through its binding rulings and clear proofs. Its wisdom is not abstract eloquence alone but includes authoritative guidance and arguments that establish its truth. This oath introduces the confirmation of Muhammad's mission that follows immediately.

phrases.translation: You ˹O Prophet˺ are truly one of the messengers
phrases.explanation: Allah confirms under oath that Muhammad is truly one of His messengers, sent with divine revelation to His servants. His mission therefore belongs to the recognized line of prophetic sending rather than being a self-appointed claim. The oath by the Quran directly supports the truth of his messenger status.

phrases.translation: upon the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: The Straight Path is Islam, a way of guidance without crookedness. The wording can describe Muhammad as sent with steadfastness upon truth or begin an independent affirmation that he stands upon this path. Both readings join his mission to straight guidance and exclude deviation from the religion he brought.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ a revelation from the Almighty, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: This revelation comes from Allah, who is almighty in retribution against disbelievers and merciful toward those who repent. Whoever turns away from disbelief and moral corruption can receive mercy rather than punishment for past crimes after repentance. Divine power and mercy together frame the purpose and warning of the revealed message.

phrases.translation: so that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned,
phrases.explanation: Muhammad was sent to warn a people who had received no warner before him, the preferred reading understanding that their forefathers lived during an interval without a messenger. Another reported reading says he warned them with the same warning given to their forefathers. The preferred interpretation explains their lack of prior direct warning without denying earlier revelation to other communities.

phrases.translation: and so are heedless
phrases.explanation: They had become heedless of what Allah does to His enemies who associate partners with Him, including the descent of His vengeance and punishment. Their heedlessness concerns consequences they had not taken seriously. Muhammad's warning addresses this unawareness by calling them to recognize both the message and the danger of persistent rejection.

phrases.translation: The decree ˹of torment˺ has already been justified against most of them, for they will never believe
phrases.explanation: The decree of punishment has become due against most of them because Allah has irrevocably recorded in the Mother of the Book that they will not believe in Him or affirm His Messenger. Their persistent rejection fulfills what He already knew and decreed. The statement concerns this particular group rather than removing the Prophet's duty to deliver warning.

phrases.translation: ˹It is as if˺ We have put shackles around their necks up to their chins, so their heads are forced up
phrases.explanation: The image depicts their right hands shackled to their necks up to the chin, forcing their heads upward and preventing them from stretching their hands toward good. It portrays complete restraint from beneficial action rather than describing an ordinary physical posture. Their moral confinement leaves them unable to reach toward the guidance they reject.

phrases.translation: and have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them
phrases.explanation: The barriers before and behind them represent being closed off from truth. Allah has made their evil deeds appear attractive, so they wander in confusion without perceiving guidance. Reports describe these barriers as errors and as separation from Islam and faith, surrounding them so that they do not penetrate to the truth.

phrases.translation: and covered them ˹all˺ up, so they fail to see ˹the truth˺
phrases.explanation: Their sight is covered by a veil, so they fail to see right guidance or derive benefit from it. This completes the image of spiritual obstruction begun with the shackles and barriers. Physical sight is not the issue, since their inability concerns recognizing and benefiting from the truth presented to them.

phrases.translation: It is the same whether you warn them or not—they will never believe
phrases.explanation: For those against whom the decree of punishment has been confirmed, the outcome is the same whether Muhammad warns them or withholds warning. They will not believe because Allah has already decreed this against them. The statement describes their settled response and does not turn the earlier command to warn into a meaningless responsibility.

phrases.translation: You can only warn those who follow the Reminder and are in awe of the Most Compassionate without seeing Him.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet's warning benefits those who believe the Quran and follow Allah's ordinances within it, while fearing the Most Compassionate even when no observers see them. Private sincerity distinguishes them from hypocrites who display faith publicly but belittle religion when alone, and from those whose sealed hearts reject guidance.

phrases.translation: So give them good news of forgiveness and an honourable reward
phrases.explanation: Muhammad should give such people good news of Allah's forgiveness for their sins and an honorable reward in the Hereafter. That reward is Paradise, granted for faithful response to the Reminder and sincere private awe. The promise addresses both removal of sin and generous future recompense.

phrases.translation: It is certainly We Who resurrect the dead,
phrases.explanation: Allah alone restores the dead to life among His creatures. This declaration places resurrection under direct divine action rather than leaving it as an uncertain possibility. It introduces the comprehensive record that will accompany people when their deeds and traces are brought into account before Him.

phrases.translation: and write what they send forth and what they leave behind.
phrases.explanation: Allah records what people send ahead of good or evil and the traces they leave, explained as their footsteps. Reports connect this with people whose homes were far from the Prophet's mosque being told that their steps were recorded. Even movements erased by wind remain included in divine knowledge.

phrases.translation: Everything is listed by Us in a perfect Record
phrases.explanation: Everything that has been or will be is enumerated in a clear Record, identified as the Mother of the Book with Allah. It makes plain the reality of what is entered in it. Deeds, footsteps, and all other matters therefore remain comprehensively recorded rather than disappearing from accountability.

phrases.translation: Give them an example ˹O Prophet˺ of the residents of a town, when the messengers came to them
phrases.explanation: Muhammad is told to present the town's residents as a lesson for his own people. Reports identify the town as Antioch but disagree over whether the messengers were disciples sent by Jesus or messengers sent directly by Allah. The account's central lesson concerns their response to the messengers, while these historical identifications remain reported possibilities.

phrases.translation: We sent them two messengers, but they rejected both.
phrases.explanation: Two messengers were sent to call the town's people to Allah, but the residents denied them both. Their rejection set the stage for additional support rather than ending the mission. The repeated denial also establishes the responsibility of the audience after receiving the initial call.

phrases.translation: So We reinforced ˹the two˺ with a third,
phrases.explanation: Allah strengthened the two envoys with a third, increasing their number and reinforcing their mission. The addition provided support after both had been rejected. Their message continued with greater strength despite the town's refusal to accept the first two messengers. Their shared testimony gained added strength.

phrases.translation: and they declared, “We have indeed been sent to you ˹as messengers˺.”
phrases.explanation: The three declared that they had truly been sent to the town's inhabitants. Their mission called people to devote worship purely to Allah alone, without any partner, and to free themselves from worshipping gods and idols. Their declaration thus concerned sincere monotheistic worship, not personal status or authority.

phrases.translation: The people replied, “You are only humans like us,
phrases.explanation: The residents objected that the three were merely human beings like themselves. They assumed that genuine envoys would have to be angels, using shared humanity as grounds to dismiss the claim. This objection attacks the messengers' nature rather than examining the truth of their call to abandon idolatry.

phrases.translation: and the Most Compassionate has not revealed anything. You are simply lying!”
phrases.explanation: They further claimed that the Most Compassionate had sent down no message or scripture and had given the three no command concerning them. On that basis, they accused the envoys of lying about being sent. Their denial rejected both the revelation and the divine authorization behind the mission.

phrases.translation: The messengers responded, “Our Lord knows that we have truly been sent to you
phrases.explanation: The messengers answer the accusation of lying by appealing to their Lord's knowledge. He knows that they were truly sent with the message to which they called the people and that they are truthful. Their confidence rests on divine knowledge of their commission rather than on their opponents' acceptance.

phrases.translation: And our duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.”
phrases.explanation: Their duty is only to convey Allah's message clearly so that the people know it has been delivered. If the audience accepts, its members benefit their own souls. If they refuse, the messengers have still fulfilled their obligation, while Allah remains responsible for judgment concerning their response.

phrases.translation: The people replied, “We definitely see you as a bad omen for us.
phrases.explanation: The residents tell the messengers that they regard them as an evil omen and would blame them for any calamity that occurred. This superstitious accusation shifts responsibility for their circumstances onto the envoys. It follows their failure to answer the call with evidence or serious reflection.

phrases.translation: If you do not desist, we will certainly stone you ˹to death˺ and you will be touched with a painful punishment from us.”
phrases.explanation: They threaten to stone the messengers and inflict painful punishment if they do not stop declaring themselves sent and rejecting the town's gods. The demand seeks to silence their prohibition of idol worship through violence. Their threat shows escalation from verbal denial to planned physical harm.

phrases.translation: The messengers said, “Your bad omen lies within yourselves.
phrases.explanation: The messengers reply that the people's deeds, sustenance, and shares of good and evil belong to them and are bound to their own responsibility. Any evil befalling them comes through what Allah has written and decreed for them, not through an evil omen carried by the envoys.

phrases.translation: Are you saying this because you are reminded ˹of the truth˺?
phrases.explanation: They ask whether being reminded of Allah is the reason the townspeople regard them as a bad omen. The question exposes the irrationality of responding to admonition with blame and threats. Receiving a reminder should prompt reflection rather than superstitious hostility toward those delivering it.

phrases.translation: In fact, you are a transgressing people.”
phrases.explanation: The messengers identify them instead as a transgressing people, disobedient to Allah and dominated by sins and excesses. Their wrongdoing lies within their own conduct rather than in the presence of the envoys. This diagnosis directly answers their attempt to make the messengers responsible for misfortune.

phrases.translation: Then from the farthest end of the city a man came, rushing.
phrases.explanation: A believing man hurried from the farthest part of the city after hearing that its people had agreed to kill the three messengers. Reports describe him as charitable and steadfast in worship despite illness and weakness. His urgent journey shows active concern to defend the messengers and warn his community.

phrases.translation: He advised, “O my people! Follow the messengers
phrases.explanation: He openly advised his people to follow the messengers Allah had sent and accept what they brought. His appeal identifies their message as guidance worth following rather than a threat. A believer from within the town now publicly counters the rejection and violence of its other residents.

phrases.translation: Follow those who ask no reward of you, and are ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: The man urges his people to follow messengers who request none of their possessions in return for guidance. Their lack of payment supports their sincerity as counselors seeking the people's welfare. They themselves stand upon the straight way of truth, so following their guidance leads others toward right guidance rather than personal exploitation.

phrases.translation: And why should I not worship the One Who has originated me,
phrases.explanation: The believer asks what possible reason he could have for refusing to worship the Lord who created him. His origin provides a direct ground for devotion to his Maker. With this question, he openly declares faith in Allah's oneness against his people's worship of idols.

phrases.translation: and to Whom you will be returned
phrases.explanation: He reminds them that they will all return and be brought back to this same Lord. Worship is therefore connected not only to their creation but also to their final return. The One who originated them remains the One before whom their lives and choices ultimately conclude.

phrases.translation: How could I take besides Him other gods whose intercession would not be of any benefit to me, nor could they save me if the Most Compassionate intended to harm me
phrases.explanation: He rejects taking other gods alongside Allah because they cannot help him if the Most Compassionate intends harm or adversity. Their intercession would not remove that harm, and they could not rescue or deliver him from it. Beings powerless in both intercession and rescue provide no rational alternative to worshipping his Creator.

phrases.translation: Indeed, I would then be clearly astray
phrases.explanation: Taking gods with such complete inability would place him in clear and manifest error. The deviation would be evident to anyone who reflected on the contrast between the powerful Creator and these helpless objects of worship. His statement treats idolatry as a departure from truth, not merely a different religious preference.

phrases.translation: I do believe in your Lord, so listen to me.”
phrases.explanation: The believer openly declares faith in the Lord whom his people had rejected and asks to be heard. Reports differ over whether he addressed his people, urging them to accept his words, or the messengers, asking them to witness his belief and adherence. Both readings preserve his public alignment with Allah and His envoys.

phrases.translation: ˹But they killed him, then˺ he was told ˹by the angels˺, “Enter Paradise!”
phrases.explanation: After his people killed him, with reports describing stoning or trampling, Allah told him to enter Paradise. Reports describe him entering alive with provision and being freed from worldly illness, grief, and weariness. His violent death was thus answered by immediate divine honor rather than by defeat or abandonment.

phrases.translation: He said, “If only my people knew
phrases.explanation: When he saw the honor Allah granted for his faith and steadfastness, he wished his people knew what had happened. He wanted them to understand that faith led to forgiveness and Paradise so that they too might believe and merit it. Even after being killed, his concern remained sincere counsel rather than revenge.

phrases.translation: of how my Lord has forgiven me, and made me one of the honourable.”
phrases.explanation: He wishes his people knew that his Lord had forgiven him and made him among the honored. A reported explanation connects this forgiveness with his faith in his Lord and affirmation of His messengers. His honor therefore confirms the very commitments for which his community rejected and killed him.

phrases.translation: We did not send any soldiers from the heavens against his people after his death, nor did We need to
phrases.explanation: Allah did not need to send heavenly armies against the believer's people after his death. The preferred explanation understands these as hosts of angels, since no such military force was required before a single cry destroyed them. Another report interpreted the statement as no further message or prophet being sent, but that reading fits the wording less directly.

phrases.translation: All it took was one ˹mighty˺ blast, and they were extinguished at once
phrases.explanation: Their destruction required only a single mighty cry sent down from heaven, after which they immediately perished. The image of being extinguished emphasizes how quickly and completely their power ended. No battle or lengthy campaign was necessary for Allah to punish those who had killed His believing servant.

phrases.translation: Oh pity, such beings!
phrases.explanation: This is an expression of grief over servants who bring regret and sorrow upon themselves by neglecting Allah's commands and falling short in their duty to Him. Their loss is self-inflicted through their response to guidance. The lament prepares for the recurring behavior summarized in the next clause.

phrases.translation: No messenger ever came to them without being mocked
phrases.explanation: Whenever a messenger from Allah came to such people, they mocked him. Their ridicule became a recurring pattern rather than an isolated response to one envoy. This habitual mockery explains the grief expressed over them and connects the town's conduct with a broader history of rejecting divine messengers.

phrases.translation: Have the deniers not considered how many peoples We destroyed before them who never came back to life again
phrases.explanation: The deniers are asked whether they have considered how many earlier generations Allah destroyed for rejecting His messengers and disbelieving in His signs. Reports mention Ad, Thamud, and many generations between them. Those peoples did not return to their former communities in worldly life, leaving their destruction as a warning to later observers.

phrases.translation: Yet they will all be brought before Us
phrases.explanation: All earlier generations, whether destroyed in worldly punishment or not, and all other people will be gathered together before Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Their absence from worldly life does not mean they have escaped His judgment. Every community will be brought into His presence without exception.

phrases.translation: There is a sign for them in the dead earth: We give it life,
phrases.explanation: Dead earth with no plants or vegetation is a sign of Allah's power. He revives it through rain sent from the sky until vegetation emerges. This observable restoration supports His ability to raise dead creatures after decay, restoring them to life just as He restores productivity to barren land.

phrases.translation: producing grain from it for them to eat
phrases.explanation: Allah brings grain from the revived earth as food and sustenance for people to eat. The sign therefore includes both revival and provision. Their daily nourishment depends upon the same divine power that transforms lifeless ground into a source of sustaining crops for their survival.

phrases.translation: And We have placed in it gardens of palm trees and grapevines,
phrases.explanation: Allah placed orchards of date palms and grapevines within the earth He revived after its barrenness. These gardens provide varied fruit and further demonstrate the richness produced through His creative arrangement. Their existence builds upon the sign of grain emerging from previously lifeless land for them.

phrases.translation: and caused springs to gush forth in it
phrases.explanation: He also caused springs of water to burst forth within the earth. These springs supply the moisture needed for cultivation and life, adding another dimension to divine provision. Water emerging from the ground complements the rain that revives it and sustains the gardens just described.

phrases.translation: so that they may eat from its fruit, which they had no hand in making.
phrases.explanation: People eat the fruits Allah brings forth from these gardens. The translation follows the permissible reading that their hands did not make the fruit, while another reading includes what they planted and sowed. Both readings recognize that human cultivation does not independently create the underlying provision Allah produces from the earth.

phrases.translation: Will they not then give thanks
phrases.explanation: After receiving food from earth Allah revived and the fruits and gardens He provided, people are asked why they will not give thanks. Gratitude should be directed to the One who bestowed these favors rather than stopping at human labor or natural processes. Provision calls for thankful recognition of its true source.

phrases.translation: Glory be to the One Who created all ˹things in˺ pairs—˹be it˺ what the earth produces, their genders, or what they do not know
phrases.explanation: Allah is glorified and declared free of imperfection as the Creator of all kinds and pairs. These include what the earth produces, male and female human offspring, and further created things people do not know. This orderly diversity contradicts the partners and inadequate descriptions that polytheists ascribe to Him.

phrases.translation: There is also a sign for them in the night: We strip from it daylight,
phrases.explanation: The night is a sign of Allah's power. He strips and draws daylight away from it, removing the day rather than merely transferring hours from one period to another. This complete withdrawal of light demonstrates His control over a recurring transition experienced by every human community.

phrases.translation: then—behold!—they are in darkness
phrases.explanation: Once daylight is removed, people find themselves in darkness through the arrival of night. The transformation is immediate and unmistakable, providing a daily sign of divine regulation. Their inability to retain daylight when Allah removes it underscores that this cycle operates under His complete command.

phrases.translation: The sun travels for its fixed term.
phrases.explanation: The sun runs toward an appointed resting place, limit, or course that it does not exceed. Reports explain this as a fixed time, a resting place under divine command, or a course extending to its furthest points of setting before returning. These explanations agree that its movement remains precisely appointed rather than uncontrolled.

phrases.translation: That is the design of the Almighty, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: This is the design and decree of Allah, who is almighty in retribution against His enemies and knows the interests of His creatures and all other matters. Nothing hidden escapes His knowledge. The sun's regulated movement therefore fully expresses both irresistible power and comprehensive awareness.

phrases.translation: As for the moon, We have ordained ˹precise˺ phases for it,
phrases.explanation: Allah determined phases for the moon as another sign, governing its waning after it reaches fullness, completeness, and roundness. Its changing appearance follows an assigned sequence rather than occurring randomly through every month. The measured progression allows people to witness order in its visible cycle.

phrases.translation: until it ends up like an old, curved palm stalk
phrases.explanation: Near the month's end, before disappearing, the waning moon becomes curved like an old, withered palm stalk. Such a stalk bends as it dries rather than remaining straight. The familiar plant image makes the moon's slender, curved final phase easy to visualize at that stage.

phrases.translation: It is not for the sun to catch up with the moon,
phrases.explanation: The sun does not overtake the moon so that its light abolishes the moon's distinct light or leaves all times as daylight without night. Each has a limit and period of dominion, with one departing as the other arrives. Their appointed succession preserves their different roles rather than merging them.

phrases.translation: nor does the night outrun the day.
phrases.explanation: Night likewise cannot outrun day so that its darkness permanently drives away daylight and leaves all times as night. The two pursue one another within fixed limits, each arriving as the other departs. This balance belongs to Allah's decree rather than arising from independent competition between them.

phrases.translation: Each is travelling in an orbit of their own
phrases.explanation: The sun, moon, night, and day each move along their appointed orbit or course. Their motion is compared to revolving or floating through a set path in the heavens. None acts outside its assigned circuit, preserving the carefully ordered succession described in the preceding signs.

phrases.translation: Another sign for them is that We carried their ancestors ˹with Noah˺ in the fully loaded Ark
phrases.explanation: Another sign of Allah's power is that He carried the descendants of Adam who were saved in Noah's fully loaded Ark. Their survival through the flood depended on divine protection and provision. The heavily laden vessel stands as historical evidence that Allah can preserve whomever He wills through overwhelming danger.

phrases.translation: and created for them similar things to ride in
phrases.explanation: Allah later created other means of riding for people as a favor. The preferred explanation identifies these as ships made after Noah's vessel, supported by the following reference to drowning at sea. Another interpretation identifies camels as ships of the land, but the immediate context of drowning makes ships the more fitting meaning.

phrases.translation: If We willed, We could drown them: then no one would respond to their cries, nor would they be rescued—
phrases.explanation: If Allah willed, He could drown people when they boarded ships at sea. No helper would answer their cries or save them from drowning, and nothing could rescue them unless Allah Himself delivered them through His mercy. Their safe travel therefore remains dependent on Him rather than guaranteed by the vessel.

phrases.translation: except by mercy from Us, allowing them enjoyment for a ˹little˺ while
phrases.explanation: Rescue occurs only through Allah's mercy, after which He allows people continued enjoyment until an appointed term, explained as death. Deliverance from drowning does not make life endless or remove later accountability. It is a temporary extension granted by the same Lord whose power could have allowed them to perish.

phrases.translation: ˹Still they turn away˺ when it is said to them, “Beware of what is ahead of you ˹in the Hereafter˺
phrases.explanation: They are told to beware what lies ahead after death, including the punishment and reckoning they will encounter if they perish in disbelief. The future consequences of their present conduct require caution before death arrives. Awareness of the Hereafter is meant to prompt a change rather than passive fear.

phrases.translation: and what is behind you ˹of destroyed nations˺
phrases.explanation: They must also heed the exemplary punishments that befell earlier communities, lest similar punishment strike them for associating partners with Allah and rejecting His Messenger. Historical destruction provides evidence of what persistent disbelief can bring. Remembering those nations turns past events into a present warning.

phrases.translation: so you may be shown mercy.”
phrases.explanation: The purpose of this warning is that they may receive mercy by repenting of polytheism, believing in Allah, and holding firmly to the obligations He imposed. Mercy is sought through genuine change and obedience. The appeal therefore offers a path back even after describing punishment before and after worldly life.

phrases.translation: Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord, they turn away from it
phrases.explanation: Whenever a sign or proof from their Lord reaches these people, they turn away from it. This includes indications of Allah's oneness and confirmation of His Messenger. They refuse to reflect or ponder long enough to understand the evidence Allah presents against them, making avoidance their settled response to revelation.

phrases.translation: And when it is said to them, “Donate from what Allah has provided for you,”
phrases.explanation: They are commanded to spend from the provision Allah bestowed upon them and pay what He imposed for the needy and destitute. Since the wealth originated as His provision, charity is a duty attached to receiving it. The command makes care for the poor part of grateful and obedient use of wealth.

phrases.translation: the disbelievers say to the believers, “Why should we feed those whom Allah could have fed if He wanted to?
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers answer by asking why they should give their wealth and food to people whom Allah could have fed Himself. They use divine power as an excuse to evade their own obligation. Instead of recognizing provision as a trust that includes duties toward the poor, they turn its unequal distribution into an argument against generosity.

phrases.translation: You are clearly astray!”
phrases.explanation: The preferred reading makes this accusation part of the disbelievers' speech, calling the believers clearly astray for urging charity. Another reading understands Allah as declaring the disbelievers astray for their objection. In either case, the dispute centers on their attempt to portray a command to feed the needy as error.

phrases.translation: And they ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”
phrases.explanation: The polytheists mockingly demand to know when the promised Hour and punishment will occur if the believers are truthful. They deny resurrection after death and hastily challenge Allah's warning rather than responding to it. Their question seeks to turn the absence of an immediately visible deadline into grounds for rejecting the promise.

phrases.translation: They must be awaiting a single Blast,
phrases.explanation: Despite their demand to hasten punishment, they await only a single mighty blast, identified as the trumpet blast of terror at the coming of the Hour. It will seize them suddenly rather than arriving according to their challenge. The awaited event is far more immediate and overwhelming than their mocking question anticipates.

phrases.translation: which will seize them while they are ˹entrenched˺ in ˹worldly˺ disputes
phrases.explanation: The blast will seize them while they remain absorbed in ordinary disputes and activities. Reports describe people haggling over garments, tending cattle, repairing troughs, displaying merchandise, and operating scales. Their preoccupation with worldly transactions will not delay the Hour or provide time to settle their affairs before it overtakes them.

phrases.translation: Then they will not be able to make a ˹last˺ will,
phrases.explanation: Once the trumpet sounds, they will be unable to make a bequest concerning the possessions in their hands. No respite will be granted for arranging inheritances or final instructions. The suddenness of destruction ends the assumption that there will always be time to put worldly affairs in order.

phrases.translation: nor can they return to their own people
phrases.explanation: Anyone away from home will also be unable to return to family or people. The same sudden event prevents both final testament and reunion with loved ones. Their ordinary movements and plans are cut off immediately, leaving no opportunity to retreat into familiar security when the Hour begins.

phrases.translation: The Trumpet will be blown ˹a second time˺,
phrases.explanation: The trumpet will be blown for resurrection. This is the blast that restores people to life after death, distinct from the earlier blast that interrupts worldly activity. The event occurs by divine command and begins the movement from death toward gathering and judgment before Allah.

phrases.translation: then—behold!—they will rush from the graves to their Lord
phrases.explanation: People will immediately emerge from their graves and hurry toward their Lord. Their rapid movement leaves no opportunity to remain behind or resist the summons. The image presents resurrection as an active rising and procession toward divine judgment rather than a return to ordinary worldly life.

phrases.translation: They will cry, “Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our place of rest?
phrases.explanation: When their souls return to their bodies after a period of sleep, the disbelievers cry out in distress and ask who raised them from their resting place. Reports describe this sleep as occurring between trumpet blasts. Their question expresses shock and ignorance as resurrection confronts them with what they denied.

phrases.translation: This must be what the Most Compassionate warned us of; the messengers told the truth!”
phrases.explanation: The declaration that this is what the Most Compassionate promised and that the messengers spoke truth is most fittingly understood as the believers' answer to the disbelievers' confused question. Another reading makes the disbelievers themselves admit it. Both interpretations confirm resurrection, accountability, and recompense as the truthful message previously delivered.

phrases.translation: It will only take one Blast,
phrases.explanation: Restoring the dead to life requires only one cry, identified as the third trumpet blast. Divine power accomplishes resurrection without a prolonged process or assistance from creation. The singular blast emphasizes the ease and immediacy with which Allah brings every single person back to life.

phrases.translation: then at once they will all be brought before Us
phrases.explanation: Everyone will then be brought together before Allah at the place of arraignment and reckoning. Not even one person remains behind or escapes presentation under any circumstance. The universal gathering includes all who were raised, ensuring that each soul enters the judgment described immediately afterward.

phrases.translation: On that Day no soul will be wronged in the least,
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will not wrong any soul. He will not withhold the full reward of a good deed or burden anyone with another person's sins. Every soul receives just treatment, with punishment limited to its own crimes and wrongdoing before Him.

phrases.translation: nor will you be rewarded except for what you used to do
phrases.explanation: People will be recompensed only for the deeds they performed during worldly life. Their actions form the basis of what they receive, without arbitrary substitution or transferred guilt between one person and another. This reinforces both complete justice and personal responsibility at the final judgment.

phrases.translation: Indeed, on that Day the residents of Paradise will be busy enjoying themselves
phrases.explanation: Paradise's residents will be occupied with joyful favors and bliss, turned away from the punishment endured by the people of the Fire. Reports variously describe delight, rejoicing, abundant enjoyment, or intimacy with virgins. The preferred explanation encompasses these forms of blessing rather than restricting their occupation to only one reported pleasure.

phrases.translation: They and their spouses will be in ˹cool˺ shade,
phrases.explanation: The people of Paradise and their spouses will be together in cool, sheltering shade. Reports describe the spouses as lawful wives among Paradise's inhabitants. The shelter is explained as freedom from exposure to the sun, adding comfort and protection to the joys already promised to them.

phrases.translation: reclining on ˹canopied˺ couches
phrases.explanation: They will recline upon couches within canopied settings. The couches are described as standing beneath bridal canopies, with mattresses and coverings arranged there. Reclining conveys rest, dignity, and ease, giving a concrete picture of the relaxed honor enjoyed by Paradise's residents and freedom from toil.

phrases.translation: There they will have fruits
phrases.explanation: Paradise's inhabitants will have fruits available to them within the Garden. This provision adds to their comfort and enjoyment after the description of shade and reclining couches. The fruit is part of the generous hospitality Allah grants them rather than something they must struggle to secure.

phrases.translation: and whatever they desire
phrases.explanation: They will also receive whatever they call for or desire. Their wishes are not restricted to the fruit explicitly mentioned, since the promise extends to what they ask. This comprehensive provision fulfills their desires within the blessing of Paradise and demonstrates the abundance of their Lord's generosity.

phrases.translation: And “Peace!” will be ˹their˺ greeting from the Merciful Lord
phrases.explanation: Peace will be a greeting and gift from their merciful Lord. Reports describe Allah greeting the people of Paradise with peace after judgment and granting their request for His good pleasure. His mercy is shown in withholding punishment for former sins and honoring them with a greeting that confirms safety and favor.

phrases.translation: ˹Then the disbelievers will be told,˺ “Step away ˹from the believers˺ this Day, O wicked ones
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers will be commanded to separate themselves from the believers on that Day. They must move toward a destination different from Paradise and enter a place unlike the believers' abode. This separation cuts them off from the good, peace, and honor just described, marking their status as wicked offenders.

phrases.translation: Did I not command you, O Children of Adam, not to follow Satan,
phrases.explanation: Allah will remind the Children of Adam that He commanded them during worldly life not to worship Satan or obey him in disobedience to Allah. The question establishes that they had already received a clear covenant and instruction. Their allegiance should have remained with their Lord rather than His opponent.

phrases.translation: for he is truly your sworn enemy
phrases.explanation: Satan's enmity was evident when he refused to prostrate before Adam out of envy for the honor Allah gave him. He then deceived Adam and his wife until they were expelled from the Garden. This history demonstrated his hostility, leaving no sound reason for human beings to follow him.

phrases.translation: but to worship Me ˹alone˺?
phrases.explanation: Allah also commanded them to worship and obey Him alone, excluding every supposed god or partner. The covenant therefore contained both a prohibition against following Satan and a positive duty of exclusive devotion. Their disobedience involved rejecting the worship they owed their Lord as well as accepting His enemy's direction.

phrases.translation: This is the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Pure devotion to Allah, obedience to Him alone, and disobedience to Satan constitute the right religion and Straight Path. This path joins belief with conduct and loyalty. It is the clear alternative to the misguidance into which Satan led those who worshipped him and other gods.

phrases.translation: Yet he already misled great multitudes of you.
phrases.explanation: Satan had already turned a great multitude away from obeying Allah and affirming His exclusive divinity. He led them to worship him and take other gods alongside Allah. Their widespread misguidance fulfilled the danger of his enmity that had already been made clear to them.

phrases.translation: Did you not have any sense
phrases.explanation: They are asked why they did not use their reason when obeying Satan and worshipping others besides Allah. Reflection should have shown them that following their own enemy and Allah's enemy was unacceptable. Their failure was not a lack of warning but a refusal to apply sound judgment.

phrases.translation: This is the Hell you were warned of
phrases.explanation: This is the Hell they were warned about during worldly life because of their disbelief in Allah and denial of His messengers. They persisted in rejecting that warning until the threatened reality stood before them. Its arrival confirms that the earlier message was neither empty nor exaggerated.

phrases.translation: Burn in it Today for your disbelief.”
phrases.explanation: They are commanded to enter and burn in Hell on the Day of Resurrection because they used to deny and reject it during worldly life. The punishment answers their persistent disbelief with the very reality they dismissed. Their former rejection no longer provides distance from the Fire they now experience.

phrases.translation: On this Day We will seal their mouths,
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will seal the mouths of those who disputed and denied the record of their actions. Reports describe people rejecting documented deeds until their ability to continue such denials is ended. Sealing their mouths concludes argument and allows other witnesses to establish the truth.

phrases.translation: their hands will speak to Us,
phrases.explanation: Their hands will speak to Allah about the disobedient actions they committed during worldly life. The limbs that performed the deeds become witnesses against their owners. Denial through speech can no longer conceal what the body itself participated in doing during the final divine reckoning.

phrases.translation: and their feet will testify to what they used to commit
phrases.explanation: Their feet will testify directly about the sins they earned and committed. Reports identify the left thigh as among the first parts to speak when mouths are sealed. This bodily testimony completes the evidence against them, leaving no successful contradiction of the deeds being judged.

phrases.translation: Had We willed, We could have easily blinded their eyes,
phrases.explanation: If Allah willed, He could obliterate their eyes as punishment for disbelief, leaving them physically blind. This is the preferred explanation because threatening to make already disbelieving people stray would add little. Another reading understands blindness to guidance, but the immediate warning more strongly supports literal loss of sight.

phrases.translation: so they would struggle to find their way. How then could they see
phrases.explanation: They might then hurry or struggle toward the path, yet without eyes they could not see where to walk or direct themselves. The rhetorical question exposes their helplessness after such punishment. For those who favor the metaphorical reading, the corresponding question is how they could find truth or guidance.

phrases.translation: And had We willed, We could have transfigured them on the spot,
phrases.explanation: Allah could also transform these people where they were, with the preferred explanation describing them fixed upon their legs in their dwellings. Another report understands the statement as destroying them in their homes. Both interpretations present a sudden act of divine power from which they could not protect themselves.

phrases.translation: so they could neither progress forward nor turn back
phrases.explanation: They would be unable to move forward or turn backward and return or find refuge. Complete immobility would prevent escape in either direction. The restriction emphasizes that human movement and freedom of action continue only through Allah's permission, which He could withdraw at any moment.

phrases.translation: And whoever We grant a long life, We reverse them in development.
phrases.explanation: Whoever receives a long lifespan eventually declines toward a condition resembling childhood through old age. Strength and knowledge can diminish until a person no longer knows what was once familiar. This reversal in physical and mental development demonstrates that human capacities change under Allah's control rather than remaining self-sustaining.

phrases.translation: Will they not then understand
phrases.explanation: People should understand Allah's power from what they visibly observe in human development. He brings a person from smallness to greatness, then permits decline after strength during old age. Such direct evidence of changing states should lead to reflection on His ability to do whatever He wills.

phrases.translation: We have not taught him poetry, nor is it fitting for him.
phrases.explanation: Allah did not teach Muhammad poetry, and it is not fitting for him to be a poet. This directly rejects attempts to classify his revealed speech as poetic composition. His prophetic role and the character of what he brought cannot be reduced to the craft attributed to poets.

phrases.translation: This ˹Book˺ is only a Reminder and a clear Quran
phrases.explanation: Muhammad is a reminder through whom Allah admonishes people and points them toward salvation. What he brought is a clear Quran that shows reflective readers it is revelation from Allah, not poetry or soothsaying. The Reminder and Book together clarify both his purpose and the message's divine source.

phrases.translation: to warn whoever is ˹truly˺ alive
phrases.explanation: The warning benefits whoever is alive in heart and sight, possessing understanding of what is said and comprehending its explanation. Such a person is intellectually and spiritually receptive rather than inwardly dead or dull. Genuine life here means the capacity to perceive and respond to admonition.

phrases.translation: and fulfil the decree ˹of torment˺ against the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: The warning also causes the decree of punishment to be justified against disbelievers who turn away from Muhammad and the guidance he brought. Their rejection establishes the case against them through their own deeds. Revelation therefore distinguishes receptive living hearts from people whose refusal confirms their liability.

phrases.translation: Do they not see that We singlehandedly created for them, among other things, cattle
phrases.explanation: The polytheists are asked to recognize that Allah created grazing livestock for the Children of Adam, including camels, cattle, and sheep. These animals exist through His creative act and are made subservient to people. Their familiar presence provides daily evidence of divine provision rather than human self-creation.

phrases.translation: which are under their control
phrases.explanation: People are given control over these animals and may manage them according to their needs. Their dominance and ability to direct livestock are themselves granted by Allah, who subjected the animals to them. Human usefulness from cattle therefore depends on both their creation and their assigned compliance.

phrases.translation: And We have subjected these ˹animals˺ to them, so they may ride some
phrases.explanation: Allah made livestock obedient and serviceable, with some animals serving as mounts. People ride camels and travel upon them over distances that would be more difficult without assistance. Their usefulness in transport is a direct result of divine subjection rather than an independently existing human entitlement.

phrases.translation: and eat others
phrases.explanation: They also eat the flesh of other livestock, receiving nourishment from animals whose creation and subjection are gifts from Allah. Meat therefore joins transport as a concrete benefit granted through these creatures. People depend on divine provision even for ordinary meals, rather than sustaining themselves independently of the Lord who made both them and the livestock.

phrases.translation: And they derive from them other benefits
phrases.explanation: Livestock supplies further benefits through wool, hair, fur, and hides. People use these materials for clothing, household furnishings, useful articles, and shelters. These varied products show that divine provision through animals extends beyond riding and meat into many necessities of ordinary life in their homes.

phrases.translation: and drinks.
phrases.explanation: They also obtain drinks from livestock, specifically milk. This nourishing drink is another direct benefit of the animals Allah created and subjected to people for their use. Mentioning drinks alongside material uses completes a picture of provision that supports human beings in several distinct ways.

phrases.translation: Will they not then give thanks
phrases.explanation: They should thank Allah for these favors by obeying Him, worshipping Him alone, and abandoning obedience to Satan and idol worship. Gratitude is therefore practical devotion rather than words alone. The proper response to receiving control, transport, food, clothing, shelter, and milk is exclusive loyalty to their Provider.

phrases.translation: Still they have taken other gods besides Allah, hoping to be helped ˹by them˺
phrases.explanation: Despite these favors, the polytheists took other gods besides Allah and worshipped them. They hoped these gods would guard them against Allah's punishment and torment. Their misplaced trust sought protection from the very Lord who had created and provided everything they used, replacing gratitude with reliance on powerless alternatives.

phrases.translation: They cannot help the pagans,
phrases.explanation: These gods cannot help their worshippers against Allah if He intends harm, nor can they ward off any adversity. The protection sought from them is therefore impossible to obtain. Their inability exposes the false expectation that devotion to idols could provide safety from divine punishment.

phrases.translation: even though they serve the idols as dedicated guards
phrases.explanation: The preferred explanation describes the worshippers themselves as a dedicated host in worldly life, growing angry and fighting on behalf of idols that bring no good and repel no harm. Another reading places their presentation at reckoning, but the idols will disown them there, making worldly partisanship the more fitting meaning.

phrases.translation: So do not let their words grieve you ˹O Prophet˺.
phrases.explanation: Muhammad should not be grieved by accusations that he was a poet or that his message was poetry, nor by their denial of Allah's signs and rejection of his prophethood. The command consoles him without denying the hostility he faced. Their statements did not alter the truth of his revelation or mission.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We ˹fully˺ know what they conceal and what they reveal
phrases.explanation: Allah fully knows what they conceal and reveal. Their hidden motivation includes envy, while inwardly they know the message is not poetry and that Muhammad is not lying. Outwardly, they publicly reject the truth with their tongues. Both their concealed recognition and open denial remain completely exposed to divine knowledge.

phrases.translation: Do people not see that We have created them from a sperm-drop,
phrases.explanation: The challenger is asked to consider that Allah created him from a mere reproductive drop and formed him into a well-shaped human being. Reports disagree over which particular opponent brought the decayed bone, but they share the central contrast between his humble created origin and his confident argument against resurrection.

phrases.translation: then—behold!—they openly challenge ˹Us˺
phrases.explanation: Despite being created in this way, he openly disputes with his Lord about the promised restoration of life after death. His challenge is public and unmistakable to those who hear it. Instead of responding to his own origin with humility, he uses it as a position from which to deny his Creator's power.

phrases.translation: And they argue with Us—forgetting they were created—
phrases.explanation: By comparing Allah to someone unable to revive decayed bones, the disputant forgets his own creation. He overlooks how Allah made him from a reproductive drop into a formed, speaking, and acting person. Reflection on that transformation would have shown him the error of measuring divine power by human inability.

phrases.translation: saying, “Who will give life to decayed bones?”
phrases.explanation: His question about who will revive decayed bones denies that they can be restored. Yet the One who originally created him can remake decayed bones into human beings in their former form. The question thus forgets the very evidence of original creation that answers its objection to resurrection.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “They will be revived by the One Who produced them the first time,
phrases.explanation: Muhammad must answer that the One who first brought the bones into existence when they were nothing will revive them. Original creation establishes the Agent and demonstrates His capability to create again. Restoration is presented as an act of the same Lord rather than an unprecedented task for an unknown power.

phrases.translation: for He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of every created being
phrases.explanation: Allah has perfect knowledge of every created being. He knows how He causes death and life and how He begins and repeats creation. Nothing concerning His creatures is hidden from Him, so decay and the passage of time do not place human remains beyond His knowledge or restorative power.

phrases.translation: ˹He is the One˺ Who gives you fire from green trees,
phrases.explanation: Allah brings forth burning fire for people from green trees. The One who produces this familiar benefit and transformation is not prevented from accomplishing whatever He wills. His ability includes reviving decayed bones and restoring them as a well-formed human being and new creation from death.

phrases.translation: and—behold!—you kindle ˹fire˺ from them
phrases.explanation: People themselves can kindle fire from these trees, making the phenomenon directly observable in ordinary life. This everyday sign supports the preceding answer about resurrection. The Creator who provides fire from green wood can also restore decayed human remains just as He originally created them.

phrases.translation: Can the One Who created the heavens and the earth not ˹easily˺ resurrect these ˹deniers˺?” Yes ˹He can˺!
phrases.explanation: The One who created the seven heavens and the earth can certainly recreate these deniers. Restoring their like from decayed bones is not greater than creating the heavens and earth. Since the greater act of cosmic creation is not impossible for Him, reviving worn bones is certainly within His power.

phrases.translation: For He is the Master Creator, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: He is the Master and Constant Creator who creates whatever He wills and does whatever He intends. He knows all that He has created and will create, with nothing hidden from Him. These attributes answer the challenge by joining unlimited creative ability with complete knowledge of every creature.

phrases.translation: All it takes, when He wills something ˹to be˺, is simply to say to it: “Be!” And it is
phrases.explanation: When Allah wills something to exist, His command is simply Be, and it comes into being. Nothing is lighter or easier than this divine command, which requires no labor or assistance. The statement completes the resurrection argument by showing that existence and restoration occur immediately through His irresistible will.

phrases.translation: So glory be to the One in Whose Hands is the authority over all things,
phrases.explanation: Allah is glorified and exalted above every deficiency. In His hand rests sovereignty over all things and their treasuries. His universal dominion encompasses every created thing mentioned throughout the chapter, confirming that no power, possession, or realm exists independently of His ultimate authority or decree.

phrases.translation: and to Whom ˹alone˺ you will ˹all˺ be returned
phrases.explanation: Everyone will return and be brought back to Allah after death. The final return places all human life under His judgment and completes the chapter's repeated emphasis on resurrection. Since dominion belongs to Him, no one can avoid returning to the One whose authority covers all things.
